about: Contract results of the TypeScript CLI on this vault, read on `today`; see test/contract/snapshot.ts. A key in differs_from_python is a result where the retired Python CLI gave something else, for the reasons of the named allowlist entries.

allowlist.block-scalar: Python refuses a block scalar (`key: |` or `key: >`). The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.comment: Python refuses a YAML comment. The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.nested-collection: Python refuses a nested map or a list inside a list. The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.anchor-or-alias: Python refuses YAML anchors and aliases. The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.quoted-typed-scalar: Python refuses a quoted value that bare YAML reads as a null, bool, or number ("true", "3"), because its serializer would drop the quotes. TypeScript keeps the quotes. The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.quoted-key: Python refuses a quoted property name. TypeScript writes it bare when bare YAML reads the same name, and keeps the quotes when it would not (`"null"`). The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.multi-line-scalar: Python refuses a plain or quoted value written across several lines. The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.escape-sequence: Python refuses double-quoted escapes other than \\ and \". The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.tab-separator: Python refuses a tab in the block; YAML allows one as a separator. The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.list-indent: Python reads list items only when indented by exactly two spaces (`  - item`); YAML also allows other indents, such as `- item` under its key. The TypeScript normalizer parses it with the yaml Document API, keeps such properties byte for byte, and returns text only after reading back the same values and comments; the harness also checks that the output keeps the values and does not change when normalized again.
allowlist.body-leading-blank-line: When the body starts with a line of only spaces, Python writes it as an extra blank line after `---`, which its own reader then drops, so normalizing again changes the note. TypeScript drops that line, so normalizing is idempotent.
allowlist.body-hard-line-break: Python trims all trailing whitespace from body lines, which deletes Markdown hard line breaks (two or more spaces before a line ending) and changes how the note renders. TypeScript keeps a final run of two or more spaces on a body line that has content (kpeez/llmos#44). The texts must differ only in those runs.
allowlist.empty-frontmatter-block: A note that starts with `---` then `---` has an empty frontmatter block. Python sees no block there (or takes the next `---` as its end), so its own canonical form of a note with no properties could not be normalized again; TypeScript reads the empty block, so normalizing is idempotent and a later stamp can add properties.
allowlist.refusal-reason: Both refuse to rewrite the note. The TypeScript message names the YAML error; the Python message names the line-parser rule.
allowlist.health-qmd-unembedded: health gained qmd_unembedded (documents still needing embedding) when the Stop hook stopped embedding; the Python health has no such field. It is null without qmd.
allowlist.message-quotes-json: Finding and schema messages quote a value as JSON, not as a Python `repr` (message wording is not contract); the quoted values and all other text must be equal.
allowlist.created-not-yyyy-mm-dd: An inbox note whose `created` is not `YYYY-MM-DD` is stale, like one without a date (Python also read `date.fromisoformat` forms such as `20261005` and `2026-W40-3`).
allowlist.properties-python-cannot-read: Python reads a note whose frontmatter it refuses (or an empty block) as having no properties; TypeScript reads the properties of valid YAML. The differences in read, list, links, topic siblings, health, and the schema audit that follow from those properties are intended. Each one is shown to follow from them: the run that reads those notes as Python does matches Python with no other difference.
